title: Prediction markets, CFTC and Don Jr.
summary: Most of the core facts hold up. TMTG announced Truth Predict in Oct 2025 and shelved it in Aug 2026 before a full launch. Don Jr. is a Kalshi strategic adviser and sits on Polymarket's advisory board, and his firm 1789 Capital invested in Polymarket. Rep. McGovern asked Selig on Apr 16, 2026 whether the White House had sought to drop a Polymarket probe. Trump posted 'It is a major industry, and we must protect it' on May 26, 2026, and the NYT reported Don Jr.'s March 2026 pitch to GOP attorneys general. The weak points: the sports-as-swaps theory predates Selig, 'on the board of both' is loose (both roles are advisory), the earlier DOJ and CFTC Polymarket probes had closed in July 2025, and no source has Don Jr. calling his remarks a 'passing comment'.

sub_claims.statement: TMTG announced Truth Predict, its entry into prediction markets, and it flopped.
sub_claims.finding: TMTG announced Truth Predict on 2025-10-28 with Crypto.com Derivatives North America as the partner. On the Q2 2026 earnings call (about Aug 7-10, 2026), interim CEO Kevin McGurn shelved it in favor of a marketing deal promoting Crypto.com's prediction products, citing a crowded market. It never fully launched, so 'flopped' means it was abandoned before launch, not that it launched and failed.

sub_claims.statement: Sports prediction markets rely on a new legal theory (sports bets as financial event contracts) that is really only possible thanks to Trump's CFTC chairman Mike Selig.
sub_claims.finding: The theory is real: the CFTC treats event contracts as CEA 'swaps' under exclusive federal jurisdiction, which would preempt state gambling law. Selig, confirmed on 2025-12-18 by a 53-43 vote, is its leading enforcer: the CFTC sued AZ, CT and IL in April 2026, later moved against other states including NY, and filed amicus briefs. But the theory predates him. Kalshi's sports contracts went live in January 2025 under Acting Chair Pham, and courts remain split, including a Nevada ruling against the platforms.

sub_claims.statement: Polymarket and Kalshi are both linked to the president's family through Don Jr., who is 'on the board of both' multibillion-dollar companies.
sub_claims.finding: Kalshi named Don Jr. a strategic adviser in January 2025; per NYT-sourced reporting, his pay included more than $300k in Kalshi shares. He joined Polymarket's advisory board on 2025-08-26, the same day 1789 Capital (where he is a partner) made a strategic investment reported as double-digit millions or eight figures. Neither role is a board-of-directors seat. The App Store finance-chart ranking was not verified.

sub_claims.statement: Selig was asked in Congress whether anyone in the White House asked him to drop the CFTC's probe into Polymarket.
sub_claims.finding: At the House Agriculture Committee hearing on 2026-04-16, Rep. Jim McGovern asked the question. Selig replied 'we treat all market participants alike' and called the insinuation 'insulting', and McGovern said 'It smells like corruption.' Context: the DOJ and CFTC had closed their earlier Polymarket probes in July 2025, before Selig. No evidence of White House interference was found.

sub_claims.statement: Kalshi's CEO could not explain why Kalshi made Don Jr. a strategic adviser ('we have a lot of advisors').
sub_claims.finding: Tarek Mansour has been questioned about Don Jr. repeatedly, including on The Axios Show in April 2026. He cites a politically diverse roster of advisers, says Kalshi 'never asked for any favors', and describes Don Jr.'s role as marketing advice. The exact clip wording was not located in text form, though the substance matches his reported answers.

sub_claims.statement: Trump posted that prediction markets are a major industry we need to protect.
sub_claims.finding: His Truth Social post of 2026-05-26 said the CFTC's 'exclusive authority over Prediction Markets' must be maintained and that 'It is a major industry, and we must protect it.' The post followed Minnesota's ban and attacked Walz, Pritzker, Letitia James and Christie.

sub_claims.statement: Don Jr. spoke to Republican state AGs and reportedly told them not to fight prediction markets.
sub_claims.finding: On 2026-08-27 the NYT, citing four people, reported that at an early-March 2026 closed-door retreat of GOP AGs in New Orleans (a Q&A with Montana AG Austin Knudsen), Don Jr. argued that federal regulators, not state AGs, should oversee prediction markets and that opposition came from gambling firms protecting 'monopolies'. Sen. Warren asked RAGA to release the transcript, and the same reporting says the White House also contacted state officials.

sub_claims.statement: Don Jr. denies it and says it was basically a passing comment.
sub_claims.finding: His spokesperson said he 'does not engage with the federal government on behalf of any company he invests in or advises'. Kalshi's 2026-08-27 rebuttal said he 'advises on marketing strategy' and 'does not advise on regulatory matters'. No source found quotes Don Jr. calling the remarks a 'passing comment'.

corrections: Transcript says 'Mike selling' and 'Seelig'; the CFTC chairman is Michael (Mike) Selig, confirmed 2025-12-18.
Transcript says 'CallSheet'; the company is Kalshi.

Transcript says Don Jr. is 'on the board of both'; he is a strategic adviser to Kalshi and on Polymarket's advisory board. Neither is a board-of-directors seat. His firm 1789 Capital invested in Polymarket.
Transcript implies Truth Predict launched and failed; it was announced in Oct 2025 and shelved in Aug 2026 before a full launch.

Transcript says sports prediction markets are 'only possible thanks to' Selig; Kalshi's sports contracts began in Jan 2025 under Acting Chair Pham. Selig is the theory's leading federal defender, not its origin.
The earlier DOJ and CFTC probes into Polymarket were closed in July 2025, before Selig became chair.
The 'passing comment' wording of Don Jr.'s denial was not found; the public denials came from his spokesperson and from Kalshi.
denials_and_context: Selig: the CFTC treats all market participants alike and does not bring politics into matters; he called McGovern's insinuation insulting.
Don Jr.'s spokesperson: he does not trade on prediction platforms and does not engage with federal officials on behalf of companies he advises or invests in.
Kalshi: Don Jr. advises on marketing, not regulation. Mansour says Kalshi never asked him for regulatory favors and points to politically diverse advisers.
TMTG: Truth Predict was dropped for competitive reasons (a crowded market), not regulatory ones.

Context cutting against the video: the CFTC's jurisdiction claim is contested in the courts, and 44 AGs (including Republicans) told the CFTC it lacks authority over sports wagering, so the policy outcome Don Jr. favors is not assured.
Context supporting the video: Sen. John Curtis (R-Utah) has called for a Senate Judiciary probe of presidential family members profiting from access, naming Don Jr.'s prediction-market ties.
